Subject: Rapid burst capacity inventory — Cascade dedicated sizing intake

Hi Sam —

Thanks again for the discussion earlier. To lock down a dedicated GPU footprint that meets your SLAs without overcommitting, we need a short inventory of traffic characteristics. I sketched the minimum fields below — attaching a sample CSV you can drop numbers into. If you can fill the first 6 rows (bolded) that will cover the sizing run.

Quick asks (high level):
- Peak concurrent sessions (p95 and p99) and the approximate peak window (start/end in your local TZ).
- Typical prompt length and typical response length (tokens). Also percent of long tails (>1024 tokens) in both prompt and response.
- Distribution by request type: conversational chat vs. single-turn generation vs. embeddings (percent).
- Average session duration and whether you use session affinity / KV cache reuse across calls.
- Desired P99 latency SLO for interactive requests and any burst-duration relaxations you accept.

Attachments: cascade_token_sample.csv (sample rows included).

If it's easier, we can schedule a 30-min probe with one of our sizing engineers tomorrow — I can bring estimated GPU SKUs based on what you send.

Thanks,
Priyom

Date: Fri, 04 Jul 2025 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Rapid burst capacity inventory — Cascade dedicated sizing intake

Priyom —

Thanks, attached a quick pass (see inline answers and attached CSV). Couple of clarifications from our side:

- Peak window: typically 11:45–12:15 PT (our highest traffic daily). We see very short micro-bursts often inside that 30min window.
- Concurrency: baseline concurrent sessions ~ 1,200; p95 ~ 3,400; p99 ~ 5,800 — but those p99 spikes are usually 10–60s long.
- Prompt/response: typical prompt 64 tokens; typical response 220 tokens. Long tails: ~4% prompts >1024, ~1% responses >1024.
- Mix: 70% chat (multi-turn), 20% single-turn generation, 10% embeddings.
- Session behavior: session affinity is on for chat; we keep KV cache per session. Average session duration (active): 8 minutes.
- SLO: target p99 inference latency 250ms for interactive (we can accept up to 600ms for long-tail responses).

CSV: cascade_traffic_export_q1.csv (attached) — it's a small sample from last Tuesday's peak.

Let me know if you want a larger dump. Also looping in procurement for timelines.

Best,
Sam
Sam Bennett | Head of AI Platform, Cascade.ai
sam.bennett@cascade.ai

-- attachment: cascade_traffic_export_q1.csv (sample rows, 200 lines)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sam Bennett <sam.bennett@cascade.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 04 Jul 2025 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Rapid burst capacity inventory — Cascade dedicated sizing intake

Sam —

Appreciate the sample and pale estimates — that helps a lot. A few immediate sizing notes from our side before we run a conservative projection:

1) Burst handling: given p99 = 5,800 with 10–60s bursts, we'll model short-duration overcommit + preemptible burst pool for 90s windows. Please confirm whether those spikes are correlated across regions (all US traffic) or if it's concentrated in a handful of tenants.

2) KV cache reuse: since you keep affinity and sessions average ~8m, we'll assume ~70% KV reuse on subsequent prompts in a session — that materially reduces per-token compute.

3) Long tail quantization: the ~4% prompts >1024 and 1% responses >1024 require fallback memory and potentially different kernel paths. We'll size a small proportion of nodes with more memory (and proactive routing) to handle those without impacting the interactive SLO.

4) Suggested next step: can we get a 48-hour sample (compressed) with fields: event_ts, prompt_tokens, response_tokens, session_id, region, request_type, latency_ms? We'll run a short telemetry decomposition and present a 3-tier plan (conservative commit + burst pool + emergency cross-region fallback).

5) Timeline: if you send the 48-hr sample by Mon EOD PT, we can have a draft footprint + SLO-risk table by Wed and a recommended reserved commit by Friday.

I've attached a quick visualization of the reported peak window (peak_window_visual.png) showing the micro-bursts.

Marissa

- Priyom: I will send a calendar invite for the probe and a short pre-read (one pager) after the call.

If procurement needs anything earlier, looping in Procurement.

Cheers,
Priyom
